title: Quantum Computing Developer
tagline: Program quantum computers and explore algorithms beyond classical limits.
about: Quantum software developers design and run quantum circuits, study quantum algorithms and build the tools around today's early quantum hardware. It's a frontier field: most roles are in research labs, hardware companies and teams exploring future applications.
Linear algebra is the entry ticket. The rest can be learned step by step with free SDKs that run real circuits.
day: Build software tools and compilers for quantum devices

phases.title: Programming foundations
phases.goal: Write small programs confidently and use the tools every developer uses daily.

nodes.d: Pick Python and get fluent with the basics before anything else. Fluency in one language transfers to every other.
links: CS50x: Harvard's intro to computer science

nodes.d: Developers live in the command line: navigating files, running programs and chaining tools together.
links: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)
OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Version control is non-negotiable: every job uses it. Commit early, branch for experiments, open pull requests.
Break problems down, read errors calmly, use a debugger and print statements deliberately.
links: Exercism: practice in 70+ languages with mentoring

phases.title: Mathematical foundations
phases.goal: The language of quantum mechanics is linear algebra.

nodes.d: Complex vectors, matrices, inner products, eigenvalues and tensor products.

links: Seeing Theory: visual probability and statistics

nodes.d: Single- and multi-qubit gates and circuit diagrams.
Write circuits in Qiskit or Cirq and run them on simulators and real devices.
Deutsch–Jozsa, Grover's search, the quantum Fourier transform, Shor's algorithm.
Today's hardware is noisy; work around it.

project.d: Implement Grover's algorithm and the QFT, run both on a simulator and a real device, and compare results with and without error mitigation.

phases.title: Applications & research
phases.goal: Where quantum might help, and how to tell.

nodes.d: Hybrid quantum-classical methods such as VQE and QAOA.
Early-stage research at the intersection with ML.
Why classical crypto is being upgraded now.

interview: Walk through an algorithm such as Grover's.
Python coding and a research discussion.
certs: IBM Certified Associate Developer – Quantum Computation using Qiskit (optional)
